With independent private values and the price equal to the second-highest exit, this mechanism is strategically equivalent to a second-price/English auction. The weakly dominant strategy is to set my sealed bid equal to my value and exit at that price. Bidding above 8 risks negative surplus; below 8 risks missing positive surplus. No history and only one round, so no signaling or shading.

[ This is effectively a sealed-bid second-price auction because the winner pays the second-highest sealed bid. With independent private values, the dominant strategy to maximize expected profit is to bid your true value. This avoids overbidding risk (negative payoff if you win above value) and underbidding risk (unnecessarily losing when price would be below value). With value 44, bid 44 to win whenever competitors’ top bid is ≤44 and pay that second-highest bid, capturing surplus equal to 44 minus that price. ]
